prompt.title: Explorer
prompt.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: extremely polished desktop application UI screenshot for "chord", a live musical Lissajous visual instrument. Landscape 16:10, high resolution, crisp legible typography. Single complete screen, no device or browser frame. It should be beautiful, enticing to play, and feasible to build.
Primary request: a gorgeous large 3D parametric curve canvas, a smaller playable circle-of-fifths chord explorer beside it, and the real MIDI Lab piano controls along the bottom. This is an expressive demo for making sounds and watching shapes, no tutorials or marketing copy.
Art direction: an exceptionally refined music instrument with deep navy-blue #0C1827 canvas, matte slate #162438 control surface, off-white #EDF1FA typography, clear ice-cyan #71DAEC, muted coral #FFAC91, soft iris #B09CF0. Highly controlled color. Beautiful proportional sans typography, modest lowercase chord wordmark. Compact functional labels, generous space around the important plot, subtle separators, restrained surface detail. Color highlights connect played notes, waveform traces and axes.
Precise layout: slim 54px header with chord wordmark left, Waveform / 2D / 3D tabs centered (3D selected), audio volume and Connect MIDI right. Below, left 24% of screen is a continuous quiet explorer panel, right 76% a large stunning plot stage. Bottom 22% a full-width playable piano dock. No duplicated controls, no unrelated metrics, no course navigation.
Explorer left panel: two compact controls across its top reading "Key  C" and "Scale  Major". Below, a beautifully drawn circular twelve-segment fifths wheel, large enough to click. Twelve outer note labels ordered clockwise from noon EXACTLY "C", "G", "D", "A", "E", "B", "F♯", "D♭", "A♭", "E♭", "B♭", "F". C segment softly cyan filled; neighboring F and G subtly highlighted. Quiet inner ring has minor labels. Center of wheel reads "C" and small "major". Below wheel a segmented choice "Chords" and "Intervals", with Chords active. Beneath, seven actual chord buttons arranged neatly in two rows: C, Dm, Em, F, G, Am, Bdim. C active with cyan accent. Next to panel footer a small "Hold" switch in active state. The panel should feel like a playable musical controller, not a lesson diagram. No explanatory prose or extra panels.
Plot stage: small "C major" label at top-left, underneath three note chips "X  C3", "Y  E3", "Z  G3" in cyan, coral, iris. The hero is a huge intricate precisely drawn 3D Lissajous trace formed by three oscillating signals approximately at ratios 4:5:6. An airy folded multi-lobed line form with crisp thin cyan/coral/iris temporal trails, subtle depth and delicate emission. It must resemble real sampled parametric curve geometry, no tubes, smoke, random particles, or planetary orbit rings. Faint perspective grid and tiny XYZ orientation gizmo. Ample empty space around the trace. A small unobtrusive live spectrum of thin semitone bars lives at stage lower-right. Three very small colored waveform traces C3/E3/G3 live along the stage lower-left, each with increasing frequency. These occupy little space.
A compact horizontal visual transport bar at bottom of plot has "Freeze", "Visual speed" slider set to "0.05×", "Trail" slider and small "Drag to orbit". Freeze independent of sound; Hold in explorer is separately visible.
Piano dock full width: a slim toolbar with searchable dropdown "Acoustic Grand Piano", small "Ch 1", "Velocity  Touch dynamics", a true toggle button "Sustain" (not a percentage slider), active "Keys" switch, and "Z / X octave" with left/right octave arrows. Underneath a beautiful flat frontal piano with ivory naturals and charcoal accidentals in correct alternating groups of TWO and THREE across THREE octaves. Do not tilt keyboard into perspective. The computer labels occur ONCE on only the middle playing range. White keys C D E F G A B C D E F have respectively A S D F G H J K L ; ' labels. Matching black keys have W E T Y U O P labels. Highlight actual C, E, G WHITE keys of the same octave in cyan, coral, iris. Footer octave labels C2 C3 C4 C5. All elements fully visible without clipping.
Hierarchy: the 3D curve is clearly the star; the wheel is the inviting second focal point; the keyboard is a real playable foundation. Make this feel like a premium live creative instrument with restrained trustworthy controls. Avoid SaaS card grids, fake statistics, large headings, decorative text, accessibility problems, bright border glows, needless labels, or excessive bloom.
